title: Impact of diafiltration buffer composition on fouling accumulation and product yield during ultrafiltration of antibody fragment fermentation permeate

record.title: Impact of diafiltration buffer composition on fouling accumulation and product yield during ultrafiltration of antibody fragment fermentation permeate
record.abstract: Diafiltration of an antibody fragment (Fab) containing fermentation permeate (initial Fab concentration 0.8 g/L, host cell protein 2.3 g/L) was performed using 30 kDa polyethersulphone membranes with five buffer compositions varying in pH (6.0–8.0), ionic strength (50–250 mM NaCl), and the presence of 0.01% polysorbate 20. Total fouling resistance after 10 diavolumes was lowest at pH 7.5, 150 mM NaCl, with polysorbate 20 (3.8 × 10¹² m⁻¹), compared with highest resistance at pH 6.0, 50 mM NaCl, without polysorbate (9.4 × 10¹² m⁻¹). Fab yield in the retentate was 88–94% across all conditions. Host cell protein clearance improved significantly at higher ionic strength, reaching 72% reduction after 8 diavolumes at 250 mM NaCl. Polysorbate 20 addition reduced surface adsorption losses without measurable impact on membrane permeability after cleaning. The results identify practical buffer formulation criteria for Fab concentration steps in downstream processing.
